Hey Folks,

This is the same i posted in John Klayer, i just thought its a new topic to start with.,

I tried a reflection hologram with HeNe-5mW laser, as John Klayer mention in his topic (By using fiber optics).

When i developed the PFG-03 with CWC2 & JD4, the emulsion started flowing away from the plate.

Within seconds, the glass plate was clear!!!. 

I just wonder why it happend, i tried with two plates, but the result was same. 

It all happend after bleaching and after we put the plate to water for rinsng. 

The point is that i created lots of holograms before with that plate before, but never had such problems before. 

I didnt used sodium sulfite with the CWC2 and the bleaching solution i used was JD4 - copper sulfate, pottassium bromide & sulfuric acid mixture.

Bathing temperature was something around 18-20 Degree C. 

One more, i live in a place where there is around 70% humidity. And now its summer here to around 30-33 degrees hot!!. 

And i forgot to put the plates in Refrigrator, i just kept them in a shelf. 

Is due to the temperature, emulsion started flowing? But then, the emulsion was alrite wen i took it for exposing. 

I am sure, there might be nothing wrong with the chemistry as i have successfully done transmission and reflection with those. 

Or i kept the solutions, i.e solution a, solution b and bleach seporately in bottles idle for around 1 month. Is that the cause? 

Or is there any guarantee period for the plates? i think the plates are less than 1 year old. 

Anybody plss tell me what might happend ?

posts.post_subject: Silver Halide Emulsion Peel of from PFG-03
posts.content_md:
Did the emulsion peel off in shreds or did it just dissolve in the water? I had PFG03 emulsion dissolve once due to accidentally rinsing in excessively warm water (I decided to rinse with cold water afterwards), but your bath temp should be OK. 

One thing to question is the use of the JD-4 bleach with CWC2 (catechol?) developer. Usually that bleach only works well with the metol-ascorbic acid developer supplied with JD-4 and a dichromate bleach is recommended for CWC2..

But if this is the same chemistry you successfuly used before with these plates, it's most likely the plates. They do apparently have a short shelf life, especially if not refrigerated.

posts.topic_title: Silver Halide Emulsion Peel of from PFG-03
posts.author: Martin
posts.post_subject: Silver Halide Emulsion Peel of from PFG-03
posts.content_md:
> **holography4fun:** Anybody tried PBQ1 or PBQ2 bleaches? Which Develper should be used with it?

I think the “PBQ1” or “PBQ2” bleaches ought to be replaced by the much safer PBU bleaches. If you use the “PBU-quinol” type, you'll actually end up with exactly the same bleaching agent, quinone (=PBQ) – without the risk of handling PBQ. Furthermore, the keeping properties of the traditional PBQ bleaches was limited to a few minutes only, whereas the PBU-quinol has a shelf live of several months.

> **Tom B:** One thing to question is the use of the JD-4 bleach with CWC2 (catechol?) developer. Usually that bleach only works well with the metol-ascorbic acid developer supplied with JD-4 and a dichromate bleach is recommended for CWC2..

I think the issue is using a reversal bleach with PFG-03 emulsions. Put aside special cases like SHSG processing, we were never able to achieve good results with reversal bleaches on PFG-03. It may be that the reversal bleach actually dissolves a large part of the undeveloped grains. Moreover silver concentration in PFG-03 is far weaker than say, in PFG-01.

posts.author: Martin
posts.post_subject: Silver Halide Emulsion Peel of from PFG-03
posts.content_md:
> **MichaelH:** Anyone have a suggestion for a substitute?

The bleach introduced by Keiler/Pollakowski, which served as the basis for Phillips/Bjelkhagen (= “PBU”), consisted of copper (II) sulfate (cupric sulfate). So I assume this would be a viable replacement for the copper bromide. Copper chloride might be another option.
